pairs.opening:
10.2 Substantial Completion
The owner approves payment when the work reaches substantial completion.
pairs.exact_quote: Such payment releases retained funds except for incomplete work.
pairs.faulty: Final payment releases retained funds except for incomplete work.
pairs.faithful: At substantial completion, payment releases retained funds except for incomplete work.
pairs.changed_element: Original retained pair; not newly constrained to a single edit
pairs.rationale: Source establishes release at substantial completion, not final payment. The latter is unestablished, not explicitly contradicted.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
5.1 Retainage release
Interim acceptance and final settlement are separate stages.
pairs.exact_quote: The owner releases retainage at interim acceptance, except amounts reserved for unfinished tasks.
pairs.faithful: Except for amounts reserved for unfinished tasks, the owner releases retainage at interim acceptance.
pairs.faulty: Except for amounts reserved for unfinished tasks, the owner releases retainage at final settlement.
pairs.rationale: The source establishes the release at interim acceptance. It does not establish the same release at final settlement.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
5.2 Release sequence
The project uses two distinct milestones named Amber and Birch.
pairs.exact_quote: Retained funds are released only at milestone Amber.
pairs.faithful: The release of retained funds occurs only at milestone Amber.
pairs.faulty: The release of retained funds occurs only at milestone Birch.
pairs.rationale: The source restricts release to Amber. Changing that milestone to Birch changes the exclusive release stage.

pairs.origin: original F3 case, unchanged; previously measured
pairs.opening:
2.1 Agreement total
The monthly agreement total covers routine services.
pairs.exact_quote: Extra visits outside the current invoice period are excluded from the agreement total.
pairs.faulty: Extra visits are excluded from the agreement total.
pairs.faithful: Extra visits are excluded from the agreement total when they fall outside the current billing period.
pairs.changed_element: Original retained pair; not newly constrained to a single edit
pairs.rationale: Removing the outside-period condition excludes visits that the clause does not exclude.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
3.2 Visit charges
The March invoice covers the monthly service period.
pairs.exact_quote: Extra visits during March are included in the March agreement total. Extra visits outside March are excluded from that total.
pairs.faithful: Extra visits outside March do not form part of the March agreement total.
pairs.faulty: Extra visits during March do not form part of the March agreement total.
pairs.rationale: The source expressly includes visits during March and excludes those outside March. The claim describes the exclusion rule only.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
3.3 Service period
Each invoice identifies the service period it covers.
pairs.exact_quote: The agreement total excludes callouts before the start of the invoiced service period; callouts within that period are included.
pairs.faithful: The agreement total does not include callouts made before the invoiced service period starts.
pairs.faulty: The agreement total does not include callouts.
pairs.rationale: The unrestricted exclusion includes in-period callouts that the source expressly includes.

pairs.origin: original F3 case, unchanged; previously measured
pairs.opening:
4.1 Failure to correct
Written notice begins the opportunity to cure a service failure.
pairs.exact_quote: If the contractor does not begin correction within seven working days after written notice and continue correction diligently, the owner may perform the correction and charge its cost to the contractor.
pairs.faulty: The owner may perform correction and charge the contractor after seven days of written notice.
pairs.faithful: If the contractor fails to start correction within seven working days after written notice and continue diligently, the owner may correct the failure and charge the contractor.
pairs.changed_element: Original retained pair; not newly constrained to a single edit
pairs.rationale: The claim drops the working-day qualifier and the failure-to-correct trigger.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
4.2 Correction notice
Written notice starts the correction clock.
pairs.exact_quote: If the contractor has not begun correction within eight working days after written notice, the owner may arrange correction and charge the contractor.
pairs.faithful: After written notice, the owner may arrange and charge for correction if the contractor has not started it within eight working days.
pairs.faulty: After written notice, the owner may arrange and charge for correction if the contractor has not started it within eight calendar days.
pairs.rationale: Changing the clock changes the trigger. The source does not establish a calendar-day deadline.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
4.3 Interrupted correction
This clause governs work that starts within the cure period.
pairs.exact_quote: If correction starts within five working days after written notice but then stops for two working days, the owner may arrange substitute correction.
pairs.faithful: If correction begins within five working days of written notice and subsequently stops for two working days, the owner may obtain substitute correction.
pairs.faulty: If correction begins within five working days of written notice, the owner may obtain substitute correction.
pairs.rationale: Starting correction alone does not establish the permission; the subsequent stop is also required.

minimal_edit.faithful_span: and subsequently stops for two working days

pairs.opening:
6.1 Property insurance
The owner maintains property insurance for the work.
pairs.exact_quote: The insurer's payment is due to the owner only to the extent the loss is covered by the property insurance policy.
pairs.faulty: The insurer's payment is due to the owner for the loss.
pairs.faithful: The insurer pays the owner only for the portion of the loss covered by the property insurance policy.
pairs.changed_element: Original retained pair; not newly constrained to a single edit
pairs.rationale: The claim drops the covered-loss limitation.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
6.2 Covered causes
The policy lists the causes of loss that it covers.
pairs.exact_quote: The insurer reimburses the owner for fire losses only; flood losses are excluded.
pairs.faithful: The owner receives insurer reimbursement only for losses caused by fire.
pairs.faulty: The owner receives insurer reimbursement only for losses caused by flood.
pairs.rationale: The faithful summary preserves fire-only coverage, including exclusion of flood. The contrast changes the covered cause.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
6.3 Water-damage coverage
An annual inspection is a prerequisite for this coverage.
pairs.exact_quote: Accidental water damage is covered only if the annual inspection is current.
pairs.faithful: A current annual inspection is required for accidental water damage to be covered.
pairs.faulty: A current annual inspection is not required for accidental water damage to be covered.
pairs.rationale: The source requires a current inspection; the contrast negates that prerequisite.

pairs.origin: original F3 case, unchanged; previously measured
pairs.opening:
8.1 Equipment use
The contractor may use the owner's equipment with permission.
pairs.exact_quote: The contractor indemnifies the owner for losses arising from equipment use, whether or not that use was negligent.
pairs.faulty: The contractor indemnifies the owner for losses from negligent equipment use.
pairs.faithful: The contractor indemnifies the owner for equipment-use losses regardless of whether the use was negligent.
pairs.changed_element: Original retained pair; not newly constrained to a single edit
pairs.rationale: Negligent-use losses are within scope, but a standalone summary omits the explicitly included non-negligent losses.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
8.2 Equipment losses
The following indemnity concerns temporary equipment.
pairs.exact_quote: The contractor indemnifies the owner for losses from both borrowed and rented equipment.
pairs.faithful: Indemnity from the contractor protects the owner against losses arising from borrowed or rented equipment.
pairs.faulty: Indemnity from the contractor protects the owner against losses arising from rented equipment.
pairs.changed_element: delete borrowed equipment from included scope
pairs.rationale: Rented-equipment losses are included, so the subset is true. It omits borrowed equipment from the standalone scope summary.

pairs.origin: new public synthetic pair; no inference
pairs.opening:
8.3 Operators
The indemnity applies regardless of which permitted operator caused the equipment loss.
pairs.exact_quote: The contractor indemnifies the owner for equipment losses caused by either employees or permitted visitors.
pairs.faithful: The owner is indemnified by the contractor for equipment losses caused by employees or permitted visitors.
pairs.faulty: The owner is indemnified by the contractor for equipment losses caused by employees.
pairs.changed_element: delete permitted visitors from included scope
pairs.rationale: Employee-caused losses are covered, but the scope summary omits permitted visitors.
